201/3-05's AFTER row: the first capture taken through the split collector, on the phone, through the panel's MCP channel with nobody relaying a number. Same link (`field`), same district, same pak and same device as the 2026-08-31 before-row.

READ THE SHAPE FIRST, because it is NOT the before-row's. The camera never moved: `map_goto` was accepted and answered `flyingTo`, but the pose in this report is still the opening one (1480,-1720 at 900 m) and only 47 of 527 drawn frames are paced - a flown window would have produced hundreds. The tab was being throttled by Android through this run (two commands went unanswered before it, the attach lapsed twice, and `map_open` had to raise the console a second time). So this is a STILL-MAP window against the before-row's flown one, and the two device numbers are not comparable with each other. That is fine for what this row is for: the before/after here is the COLLECTOR, and both sides of it are computed from this one capture's own data.

THE BEFORE/AFTER, on one window, arithmetic rather than assertion. The old collector kept every dt in one population, so its numbers for THIS capture would have been: dtMean over all 527 samples = (49797 rest + 47 x 33.76 paced) / 527 = 97.5 ms; p50 over all 527 lands at index 263, and since only 46 samples fall below 100 ms the median is a rest interval at ~103 ms; so `fps` = round(1000/103) = **10**. What it reports now, over the 47 intervals that are frame times: **p50 28 ms, fps 36**, p95 76, max 104.7. The same window, off by 3.6x, and the old number was the render gate's idle poll wearing a frame rate's name.

AND THE REST POPULATION IS NAMED RATHER THAN DERIVED. `rest` says 480 frames, mean **103.74 ms**, total 49 797 ms - which is 82 % of the 60.7 s window, and 103.74 is IDLE_WAKE_MS plus the loop prologue, measured directly for the first time. Every row from 2026-08-22 to 08-31 picked this out of the histogram by hand in its own prose; nothing has to now.

STILL WRONG, FOUND BY THIS RUN, one layer further down: **the CPU block is diluted the same way the dt block was.** `cpu.bodyMs` is paired one frame late on purpose (the body that ran inside the interval being reported is the previous pass's) - but when the previous pass was SKIPPED, that body is the skipped pass's ~0.2 ms, not a frame's. So `bodyMeanMs` 1.48 ms is 480 skip bodies averaged in with 47 real ones. The true paced body is recoverable from `shareOfFrame` x `dtMeanMs` = 0.410 x 33.76 = **13.84 ms**, a 9.3x dilution, and `segmentsMs` is divided by 527 instead of 47 so every segment is ~11x low (`overlay-2d` reads 0.70 ms against a real ~7.9). `shareOfFrame` and `outsideMeanMs` are already correct because they were restricted to the paced population - which incidentally fixed their pairing too, since a paced frame's previous pass drew. The old collector would have reported shareOfFrame = 1.483 / 97.5 = **1.5 %** here; it reads 41 %. Do not quote `bodyMeanMs` or `segmentsMs` from this row.

The on-screen counter agrees in shape with the capture, which is the point of giving both one owner: `frameMs` 23.6 ms and `cpuMs` 12.5 ms against the capture's p50 28 and recovered paced body 13.84.

App `fd0c8ae+` - built from the working tree that became a78a0f8, so the '+' is the proof this ran the split collector. Device MGA-LX3 / ARM Bifrost, 360x320 CSS at DPR 2 (the sheet was open, so the map had 320 px of height), no timestamp-query so GPU time is not measurable. Pak: original, district los-santos-centre, textures astc, built 19:23 28-08-2026.
